AuthiChain's product passports resolve through GS1 Digital Link URI Syntax — the URI grammar GS1 publishes for encoding product identifiers in a scannable link, and the syntax GS1 recommends for the EU Digital Product Passport's data-carrier requirement. A code encodes /01/{gtin}/21/{serial}: application identifiers any GS1-conformant resolver already knows how to parse, not a URL scheme we invented for ourselves.

Content negotiation decides what you get back. Point a browser at the link and it redirects to a passport page. Send the same URL with an Accept: application/json header and you get structured data instead — GTIN, lot, serial, chain and contract address, scan history — no proprietary app required to read it.

Each passport status ships with an explicit boundary rather than a bare label. "Active" means the identifier is registered and the scan pattern is consistent with a single unit — the status copy states directly that this says nothing about manufacturing quality. "Not found" means the identifier isn't in the registry, and says so plainly: absence isn't proof of counterfeit by itself, it can be an unregistered genuine item. Six states, each paired with what it proves and what it explicitly doesn't.

Clone detection works off scan velocity and geographic spread: the same serial scanned across several regions inside a short window moves a seal from active to clone_suspected, then cloned. That's a pattern on a scan graph, not a forensic finding on the object — the geolocation behind it is country-level plus an optional Cloudflare colo, not GPS, and it's flagged as a risk signal to go inspect, not a verdict.

Spec and status definitions: https://authichain.com/spec

reddit.title: Our product QR codes use the GS1 Digital Link URI syntax, not a custom scheme — any GS1-conformant resolver can already parse them
reddit.body:
AuthiChain issues per-unit product passports reachable by scanning a QR code. This week we wired the passport route to the GS1 Digital Link URI Syntax — the official GS1 URI grammar — instead of a URL format we made up: a code encodes application identifiers in the path, e.g. /01/{gtin}/21/{serial}, with lot (10), expiry (17) and production date (11) also supported.

Why that matters here specifically: GS1 maintains the GTIN/lot/serial identifiers used across most physical retail supply chains, and GS1 Digital Link is the URI syntax GS1 recommends for the EU's Digital Product Passport carrier requirement. Building on it instead of a proprietary path format means the code on the label is legible to any GS1-conformant resolver, not locked to our redirect service.

Content negotiation decides what you get back. Hit the link in a browser and you're redirected to a human passport page. Hit it with Accept: application/json (or the /v1/passport/{id} path directly) and you get structured JSON — GTIN, lot, serial, chain/contract/tx if minted, and scan history.

The part I'd actually want pushback on: clone detection. A seal moves issued → active → clone_suspected → cloned based on scan velocity and how many distinct regions scan the same serial inside a rolling window. It's a heuristic on a scan graph, and the status copy says so directly — "not a courtroom finding, treat as a risk flag and inspect the item." The geolocation behind it is country plus an optional Cloudflare colo, not GPS, and there's no tx hash on a seal until it's actually minted on-chain.

Parser and state machine are both plain TypeScript with no dependencies, sitting in the repo if anyone wants to see how the region/velocity scoring works or find where the AI-element parsing gets it wrong.

https://authichain.com/eu-dpp

Disclosure: I work on this project.
